best_for: Windows 10 and 11 power users who want a free keyboard launcher for apps, files and web searches, and who like adding plugins.

points.title: One hotkey for most jobs
points.text: Type to open apps, find files, run web searches, open bookmarks, do quick math or run shell commands, including as administrator. System commands like lock, sleep and shutdown sit in the same box.

points.title: File search is borrowed
points.text: It searches file names and file contents through either Everything or the Windows Search index, so results are only as good as the index you pick.

points.title: Plugins from a built-in store
points.text: Install plugins from the Plugin Store in settings or with the `pm` command in the search box. They can be written in C#, F#, Python or Node.js.

points.title: Free, MIT licensed, still fixing details
points.text: Flow Launcher is open source under the MIT license. Version 2.1.4 was a bug-fix release, with better handling of quoted shell commands and Windows Terminal launches, and it dropped ftp:// links.

points.title: Expect a security warning
points.text: The code is not signed, so Windows may warn you on first run. It is not in the Microsoft Store yet.

points.title: Per-user, with a portable mode
points.text: The installer listed here is a 32-bit build that installs for the current user. A portable mode keeps settings in a UserData folder next to the app instead of in AppData. This site keeps 44 Windows versions.
